title: Christopher and Cosmas, taken by Cavendish, 1587–c. 1591
summary: Two Japanese youths, about 20 and 16 and known only by their Christian names, were taken off the Manila galleon Santa Ana when Thomas Cavendish captured it off Baja California on 4 November 1587. They went with him across the Pacific and Indian Oceans to England, stayed there perhaps three years, and sailed again with him in 1591. They are not heard of after that.

events.label: Taken off the Santa Ana
events.text: Cavendish’s Desire and Content caught the Manila galleon Santa Ana at Bernabe Bay, about 20 miles east of Cabo San Lucas, put its crew ashore, took the cargo and burned the ship. Christopher, about 20, and Cosmas, about 16, went with the English.

events.label: Out again with Cavendish
events.text: Cavendish left Plymouth for Brazil. Samuel Purchas mentions the two in Antonie Knivet’s account of this voyage. Nothing is recorded of them after it.

events.label: Fate unknown
events.text: The page says they are not mentioned again and probably died when Cavendish’s Lester was lost after St Helena. The place is a guess.
events.doubt: No source records how or where either died; this mark is St Helena, the last place the page names before the loss; where the ship was lost is unknown.
